subject: long fingernails
title: What If You Never Cut Your Nails? Unlike Hair, They Never Stop

scenes.text: What if you never cut your nails again? Hair would eventually stop. Nails never do.
Fingernails grow about three and a half millimetres a month. After a year, each one is four centimetres longer.
Hair grows in cycles and falls out at a set length. Nails have no resting phase. They just keep coming.
After ten years, each nail is over 40 centimetres, twisting into spirals.
One woman stopped cutting in 1997. In 2022 her ten nails measured 13 metres combined. Painting one takes five hours.
Your toenails would lag at half the speed. But they'd never stop either. Not for as long as you live.

description:
What if you never cut your nails? Fingernails grow about 3.5 millimetres a month and toenails about 1.6, and, unlike hair, nails have no resting phase, so they never stop.
Diana Armstrong has not cut hers since 1997; in 2022 Guinness measured them at over 13 metres combined, the longest ever. Painting a single nail takes her about five hours.
